A sweet tea from Taiwan, usually milk tea, served cold with chewy balls of tapioca that you drink through a wide straw. It appeared in the 1980s; two tea houses, Chun Shui Tang in Taichung and Hanlin in Tainan, both claim to have invented it.

It mixes ingredients from far apart. The tea goes back to Chinese tea culture, set down in works like The Classic of Tea. The tapioca comes from cassava, a root crop first grown in South America and brought to Asia by Europeans. Taiwan's night markets and tea stands made it a cheap everyday treat.

From the late 1990s it spread with Taiwanese and Chinese migrants to Hong Kong, Southeast Asia, North America and Europe. Shops now sell it around the world, with fruit teas, jellies and many other toppings. It is one of the most visible exports of modern Taiwanese food culture.
